title.zh: 卷七 列傳第一: 皇后
title.raw: 卷七 列傳第一: 皇后 Volume 7: Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 陳書卷七

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 7
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 7

sentences.zh: 列傳第一

translations.literal: Biographies, Number One
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part One

sentences.zh: 高祖章皇后 世祖沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 高宗柳皇后

translations.literal: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu
translations.idiomatic: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu

sentences.zh: 後主沈皇后 張貴妃

translations.literal: Last Emperor Empress Shen; Noble Consort Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Last Emperor Empress Shen; Noble Consort Zhang

sentences.zh: 周禮，王者立后，六宮，三夫人，九嬪，二十七世婦，八十一御妻，以聽天下之內治。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the king establishes a queen, the Six Palaces, three consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendant wives to hear and govern inner affairs throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say that a king establishes a queen, the Six Palaces, three chief consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendant wives to govern the inner realm.

sentences.zh: 然受命繼體之主，非獨外相佐也，蓋亦有內德助焉。

translations.literal: Yet rulers who receive the Mandate and succeed to the line are aided not only by ministers without; surely inner virtue assists as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rulers who receive the Mandate and succeed to the throne are aided not only by ministers without, but also by virtue within.

sentences.zh: 漢魏已來，六宮之職，因襲增置，代不同矣。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward the offices of the Six Palaces were inherited and increased, and each age differed.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward the offices of the Six Palaces were carried on and expanded, and no two dynasties were alike.

sentences.zh: 高祖承微接亂，光膺天歷，以朴素自處，故後宮員位多闕。

translations.literal: The Founder received the succession amid turmoil and disorder and brightly bore Heaven's calendar; because he kept himself in plain simplicity, many posts in the inner palace stood vacant.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder took the throne amid turmoil and lived plainly, so many posts in the inner palace went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 世祖天嘉初，詔立後宮員數，始置貴妃、貴嬪、貴姬三人，以擬古之三夫人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia under Emperor Wen, an edict fixed the number of inner-palace posts; for the first time three offices were established—noble consort, noble concubine, and noble lady—to match the ancient three consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1 (562) Emperor Wen fixed the number of inner-palace posts and for the first time created three offices—noble consort, noble concubine, and noble lady—to match the ancient three chief consorts.

sentences.zh: 又置淑媛、淑儀、淑容、昭華、昭容、昭儀、[1]脩華、脩儀、脩容九人，以擬古之九嬪。

translations.literal: There were also established nine persons: Shuyuan, Shuyi, Shurong, Zhaohua, Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, Editorial footnote marker 1. Xiuhua, Xiuyi, and Xiurong, to match the ancient nine concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed nine women—Shuyuan, Shuyi, Shurong, Zhaohua, Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, [1] Xiuhua, Xiuyi, and Xiurong—to match the ancient nine concubines.

sentences.zh: 又置婕妤、容華、充華、承徽、烈榮五人，謂之五職，亞於九嬪。

translations.literal: There were also established five offices—Jieyu, Ronghua, Chonghua, Chenghui, and Lierong—called the Five Duties, ranking below the nine concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He also created five offices—Jieyu, Ronghua, Chonghua, Chenghui, and Lierong—the Five Duties, ranking below the nine concubines.

sentences.zh: 又置美人、才人、良人三職，其職無員數，號為散位。

translations.literal: There were also established three offices—Beauty, Talent, and Good Wife—with no fixed quota for their posts; they were called scattered ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He also created three offices—Beauty, Talent, and Good Wife—with no fixed quota; they were called scattered ranks.

sentences.zh: 世祖性恭儉，而嬪嬙多闕，高宗、後主內職無所改作。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature respectful and frugal, yet many concubines' posts still stood vacant; Emperor Xuan and the Last Emperor made no changes to the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was respectful and frugal, and many concubines' posts still went unfilled; Emperor Xuan and the Last Emperor changed nothing in the inner offices.

translations.literal: (order)
translations.idiomatic: (order)

sentences.zh: [今]之所綴，[2]略備此篇。

translations.literal: [Now] what is compiled here, Editorial footnote marker 2. briefly supplies this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: [Now] what is compiled here [2] briefly supplies this chapter.

sentences.zh: 高祖皇后章要兒

translations.literal: Founder Empress Zhang Yaor
translations.idiomatic: Founder Empress Zhang Yaor

sentences.zh: 高祖宣皇后章氏，諱要兒，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: The Founder's Empress Xuan, of the Zhang clan, personal name Yaor, was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xuan, empress of the Founder, of the Zhang clan, was named Yaor and came from Wucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 本姓鈕，父景明為章氏所養，因改焉。

translations.literal: Her original surname was Niu; her father Jingming was adopted by the Zhang clan and therefore changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Her family had borne the surname Niu; her father Jingming was adopted by the Zhang clan and took their name.

sentences.zh: 景明，梁代官至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Jingming under Liang reached the office of scattered-cavalry gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Jingming had served Liang as scattered-cavalry gentleman.

sentences.zh: 后母蘇，嘗遇道士以小龜遺己，光采五色，曰：「三年有徵。

translations.literal: The empress's mother Su once met a Daoist who gave her a small turtle with a five-colored radiance, saying, "In three years there will be a sign."
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Su once met a Daoist who gave her a small turtle glowing in five colors and said, "In three years there will be a sign."

sentences.zh: 」及期，后生而紫光照室，因失龜所在。

translations.literal: When the term arrived, the empress was born and purple light filled the chamber; the turtle's whereabouts were then lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, the empress was born and purple light filled the room; the turtle was nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧，美容儀，手爪長五寸，色嵭紅白，每有硋功之服，則一爪先折。

translations.literal: In youth she was clever and quick, with a beautiful bearing; her fingernails were five inches long, reddish and white in color, and whenever there were mourning garments that hindered work, one nail would break first.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she was clever and beautiful; her fingernails were five inches long, reddish white, and whenever she wore mourning garments that got in the way, one nail would snap first.

sentences.zh: 高祖先娶同郡錢仲方女，早卒，後乃聘后。

translations.literal: The Founder first married a daughter of Qian Zhongfang of the same commandery, who died early; afterward he betrothed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had first married a daughter of Qian Zhongfang of the same commandery, who died young; only then did he betroth the empress.

sentences.zh: 后善書計，能誦詩及楚辭。

translations.literal: The empress was skilled at writing and reckoning and could recite the Odes and the Songs of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was skilled at writing and reckoning and could recite the Odes and the Songs of Chu.

sentences.zh: 高祖自廣州南征交阯，命后與衡陽王昌隨世祖由海道歸于長城。

translations.literal: When the Founder from Guangzhou campaigned south against Jiaozhi, he ordered the empress to follow Prince of Hengyang Chang with Emperor Wen by the sea route back to Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched from Guangzhou against Jiaozhi, he sent the empress with Prince of Hengyang Chang and Emperor Wen home by sea to Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖下至豫章，后為景所囚。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder went down to Yuzhang; the empress was imprisoned by Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder went down to Yuzhang, and the empress was taken prisoner by Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，而高祖為長城縣公，后拜夫人。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified and the Founder became Duke of Changcheng county, the empress was invested as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing fell and the Founder became Duke of Changcheng, the empress was made his lady.

sentences.zh: 及高祖踐祚，永定元年立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, in the first year of Yongding she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, in Yongding year 1 (557) she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 追贈后父景明特進、金紫光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，拜后母蘇安吉縣君。

translations.literal: The empress's father Jingming was posthumously promoted to special grand master and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, with a golden seal and purple cord added; the empress's mother Su was invested as Lady of Anji county.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Jingming was posthumously made special grand master and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon; her mother Su was made Lady of Anji county.

sentences.zh: 二年，安吉君卒，與后父合葬吳興。

translations.literal: In the second year the Lady of Anji died and was buried with the empress's father in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Lady of Anji died and was buried with the empress's father in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 明年，追封后父為廣德縣侯，邑五百戶，謚曰溫。

translations.literal: The next year the empress's father was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde county with a fief of five hundred households; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year her father was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde with five hundred households; his posthumous title was Wen.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，后與中書舍人蔡景歷定計，祕不發喪，召世祖入纂，事在蔡景歷及侯安都傳。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, the empress with Masters of Writing Attendant Cai Jingli settled the plan, kept the death secret, and summoned Emperor Wen to succeed; the matter is in the biographies of Cai Jingli and Hou Andu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died, the empress and masters of writing attendant Cai Jingli laid their plans, kept the death secret, and summoned Emperor Wen to succeed; the affair is told in the biographies of Cai Jingli and Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰慈訓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Cixun.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Cixun.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊后為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the empress was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，后下令黜廢帝為臨海王，命高宗嗣位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda the empress issued an order deposing the Deposed Emperor as Prince of Linhai and appointing Emperor Xuan to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 2 (569) she issued an order deposing the Deposed Emperor as Prince of Linhai and installing Emperor Xuan in his place.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，尊后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian she was again honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) she was again honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 二年三月景申，崩于紫極殿，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the second year, third month, day renshen, she died in the Hall of Purple Apex at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taijian year 2 (570), on day renshen, she died in the Hall of Purple Apex at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 遺令喪事所須，並從儉約，諸有饋奠，不得用牲牢。

translations.literal: Her final command was that all funeral needs be kept frugal and simple, and that offerings presented at the mourning must not use oxen or sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Her last command was that the funeral be kept frugal and that no offerings of oxen or sheep be used.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，羣臣上謚曰宣太后，祔葬萬安陵。

translations.literal: That year, fourth month, the ministers submitted the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuan; she was buried with the Founder at Wan'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month the ministers gave her the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuan; she was buried with the Founder at Wan'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 后親屬無在朝者，唯族兄鈕洽官至中散大夫。

translations.literal: None of the empress's close kin held office at court; only a clansman of the same surname, Niu Zhi, reached the post of palace gentleman of the central staff.
translations.idiomatic: None of the empress's close kin held office at court; only a clansman, Niu Zhi, rose to palace gentleman of the central staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖皇后沈妙容

translations.literal: Emperor Wen Empress Shen Miaorong
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen Empress Shen Miaorong

sentences.zh: 世祖沈皇后諱妙容，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's Empress Shen, personal name Miaorong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's empress Shen, named Miaorong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父法深，梁安前中錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Her father Fashen under Liang was recorder of the Prince of An's front headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Fashen had served Liang as recorder of the Prince of An's front headquarters.

sentences.zh: 后年十餘歲，以梁大同中歸于世祖。

translations.literal: When the empress was a little more than ten years old, in the Datong era of Liang she was married to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When she was barely ten, in the Datong era of Liang she was married to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 高祖之討侯景，世祖時在吳興，景遣使收世祖及后。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing, Emperor Wen was then in Wuxing; Jing sent envoys to seize Emperor Wen and the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder moved against Hou Jing, Emperor Wen was in Wuxing; Jing sent men to seize him and the empress.

sentences.zh: 景平，乃獲免。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, they were then released.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing fell they were freed.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，永定元年，后為臨川王妃。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, in the first year of Yongding the empress became Princess of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, in Yongding year 1 (557) she became Princess of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, she became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 追贈后父法深光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，封建

translations.literal: The empress's father Fashen was posthumously promoted to grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian
translations.idiomatic: Her father Fashen was posthumously made grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian

translations.literal: (success)
translations.idiomatic: (success)

sentences.zh: [城]縣侯，[3]邑五百戶，謚曰恭，追贈后母高綏安縣君，謚曰定。

translations.literal: [cheng] county, Editorial footnote marker 3. fief five hundred households, posthumous title Gong; the empress's mother Gao was posthumously invested as Lady of Anji county, posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: [cheng] county, [3] with a fief of five hundred households and posthumous title Gong; her mother Gao was posthumously made Lady of Anji county with posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰安德。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Ande.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Ande.

sentences.zh: 時高宗與僕射到仲舉、舍人劉師知等並受遺輔政，師知與仲舉恆居禁中參決红事，而高宗為揚州刺史，與左右三百人入居尚書省。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan, together with Vice Director Dao Zhongju, Attendant Liu Shizhi, and others, all received the testament and assisted in government; Shizhi and Zhongju constantly dwelt within the forbidden quarters deciding military affairs, while Emperor Xuan was Inspector of Yangzhou and entered the Masters of Writing office with three hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuan, with vice director Dao Zhongju, attendant Liu Shizhi, and others, shared the testament and governed; Shizhi and Zhongju lived in the inner palace and decided affairs of state, while Emperor Xuan was inspector of Yangzhou and lodged in the masters of writing office with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 師知見高宗權重，陰忌之，乃矯队謂高宗曰：「今四方無事，王可還東府，經理州務。

translations.literal: Shizhi saw Emperor Xuan's power growing and secretly resented him; he therefore forged an order and told Emperor Xuan, "Now the four quarters are at peace; Your Highness may return to the Eastern Mansion and manage the prefecture's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi saw Emperor Xuan's power growing and secretly feared him; he forged an order saying, "The realm is at peace; you may return to the Eastern Mansion and mind the prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」高宗將出，而諮議毛喜止之曰：「今若出外，便受制於人，譬如曹爽，願作富家翁不可得也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to go out when Adviser Mao Xi stopped him and said, "If you go out now you will be subject to others—as with Cao Shuang, you may wish to be a rich householder yet cannot obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was about to leave when adviser Mao Xi stopped him and said, "Go out now and you fall under another's hand—as with Cao Shuang, you may wish only to be a rich man and cannot even have that."

sentences.zh: 」高宗乃稱疾，召師知留之與語，使毛喜先入言之於后。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan then claimed illness, summoned Shizhi and detained him to talk, and sent Mao Xi in first to speak to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then feigned illness, summoned Shizhi and kept him talking, and sent Mao Xi ahead to speak to the empress.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「今伯宗年幼，政事並委二郎，此非我意。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Now Bozong is young; all government is entrusted to the Second Lord—this is not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Bozong is still young; to put all government in the Second Lord's hands is not my wish."

sentences.zh: 」喜又言於廢帝，帝曰：「此自師知等所為，非朕意也。

translations.literal: Xi also spoke to the Deposed Emperor; the emperor said, "This was done by Shizhi and the others alone; it is not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Xi also spoke to the Deposed Emperor, who said, "That was Shizhi and his party—not my wish."

sentences.zh: 」喜出以報高宗，高宗因囚師知，自入見后及帝，極陳師知之短，仍自草敕請畫，以師知付廷尉治罪。

translations.literal: Xi went out and reported to Emperor Xuan; Emperor Xuan therefore imprisoned Shizhi, entered in person to see the empress and the emperor, set forth Shizhi's faults at length, himself drafted the edict and requested the seal, and handed Shizhi over to the Court of Trials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi came out and told Emperor Xuan, who then seized Shizhi, went in to see the empress and the emperor, laid out Shizhi's crimes, drafted the edict himself, and sent Shizhi to the court of trials.

sentences.zh: 其夜，於獄中賜死。

translations.literal: That night he was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was granted death in prison.

sentences.zh: 自是政無大小，盡歸高宗。

translations.literal: From then on, whether affairs were great or small, all fell to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, great and small alike, all power passed to Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 后憂悶計無所出，乃密賂宦者蔣裕，令誘建安人張安國，使據郡反，冀因此以圖高宗。

translations.literal: The empress, worried and distressed with no plan, secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to induce Zhang Anguo of Jian'an to hold the commandery in rebellion, hoping thereby to strike at Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, anxious and at her wits' end, secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to stir Zhang Anguo of Jian'an into holding the commandery in rebellion, hoping thus to move against Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 安國事覺，並為高宗所誅。

translations.literal: When Anguo's affair was discovered, all were executed by Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Anguo's plot was discovered, Emperor Xuan had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 時后左右近侍頗知其事，后恐連逮黨與，並殺之。

translations.literal: At that time the empress's close attendants largely knew of the affair; fearing that their associates would be seized together, she had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Her close attendants largely knew of the plot; fearing they would be seized with their associates, she had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以后為文皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, the empress was made Empress Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, the empress was titled Empress Wen.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，大業初，自長安歸于江南，頃之，卒。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and entered Sui, in the early Daye era she returned from Chang'an to the southland; before long she died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell to Sui, in the early Daye era she returned from Chang'an to the south; soon she died.

sentences.zh: 后兄欽，隨世祖征伐，以功至貞威將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Qin followed Emperor Wen on campaign and for merit reached the post of steadfast-prestige general and Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder brother Qin followed Emperor Wen on campaign and for merit rose to steadfast-prestige general and inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，襲爵建城侯，加通直散騎常侍、持節、會稽等九郡諸軍事、明威將軍、會稽太守，入為侍中、左纫將軍、纫尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, [Qin] inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Jiancheng, was promoted to supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication, given credentials, made area commander of the nine commanderies including Kuaiji, bright-prestige general, and Kuaiji Administrator; he entered court as palace attendant, left guard general, and guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Qin inherited the marquisate of Jiancheng, was made supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication with credentials, area commander of nine commanderies including Kuaiji, bright-prestige general, and Kuaiji administrator, then entered court as palace attendant, left guard general, and guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 光大中，為尚書右僕射，尋遷左僕射。

translations.literal: In the Guangda era he was right vice director of the masters of writing; soon he was transferred to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangda era he was right vice director of the masters of writing, then left vice director.

sentences.zh: 欽素無技能，奉己而已。

translations.literal: Qin by nature had no skill; he looked only to his own comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had no talent and cared only for his own ease.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，出為雲麾將軍、義興太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Qin] went out as cloud-banner general and Administrator of Yixing, salary at two thousand shi of the middle rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Qin went out as cloud-banner general and administrator of Yixing at two thousand shi of the middle rank.

sentences.zh: 太建元年卒，時年六十七，贈侍中、特進、翊左將軍，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he died at age sixty-seven; he was posthumously given palace attendant, special grand master, and left assistant general, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he died at sixty-seven; he was posthumously made palace attendant, special grand master, and left assistant general, with posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子觀嗣，頗有學識，官至御史中丞。

translations.literal: His son Guan succeeded him; he had considerable learning and reached the post of imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan succeeded him; Guan was learned and rose to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 廢帝王皇后

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Empress Wang
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Empress Wang

sentences.zh: 廢帝王皇后，金紫光祿大夫固之女也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor's Empress Wang was a daughter of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor's empress Wang was a daughter of grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon Gu.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，為皇太子妃，廢帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia she became crown princess; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1 (562) she became crown princess; when the Deposed Emperor succeeded she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 廢帝為臨海王，后為臨海王妃。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor became Prince of Linhai, the empress became Princess of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor was made Prince of Linhai, she became Princess of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 至德中薨。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era she died.

sentences.zh: 高祖柳皇后

translations.literal: Founder Empress Liu
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan Empress Liu

sentences.zh: 后性謙謹，未嘗以宗族為請，雖衣食亦無所分遺。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature modest and cautious; she never made requests on behalf of her clan, and even in food and clothing she gave them nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was modest and cautious; she never asked favors for her clan and shared neither food nor clothing with them.

sentences.zh: 弟盼，太建中尚世祖女富陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Pan in the Taijian era married Emperor Wen's daughter Princess of Fuyang and was appointed commandant of the emperor's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Pan in the Taijian era married Emperor Wen's daughter, Princess of Fuyang, and was made commandant of the emperor's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，以帝舅加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, as the emperor's maternal uncle he was promoted to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor succeeded, as the emperor's uncle by marriage he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 盼性愚戇，使酒，常因醉乘馬入殿門，為有司所劾，坐免官，卒於家。

translations.literal: Pan was dull and foolish, fond of wine; he often rode his horse drunk through the palace gate and was impeached by the responsible offices, stripped of office, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was dull and fond of drink; drunk, he often rode through the palace gate, was impeached, dismissed, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中護軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given palace attendant and central guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and central guard commander.

sentences.zh: 後主皇后沈婺華

translations.literal: Last Emperor Empress Shen Wuhua
translations.idiomatic: Last Emperor Empress Shen Wuhua

sentences.zh: 后無子，養孫姬子胤為己子。

translations.literal: The empress had no son; she adopted Sun Ji's son Yin as her own child.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had no son; she adopted Sun Ji's son Yin as her own.

sentences.zh: 后宗族多有顯官，事在君理傳。

translations.literal: Many in the empress's clan held eminent office; the matter is in the biography of Junli.
translations.idiomatic: Many of her clan held high office; their stories are in the biography of Junli.

sentences.zh: 后叔君公，自梁元帝敗後，常在江陵。

translations.literal: The empress's uncle Jun Gong, after Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated, remained constantly at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Jun Gong, after Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated, stayed at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，與蕭瓛、蕭巖率红叛隋歸朝，後主擢為太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era, together with Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan he led their followers in defecting from Sui and returning to court; the Last Emperor promoted him to grand mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenming era he and Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan led their men in defecting from Sui back to Chen; the Last Emperor made him grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 君公博學有才辯，善談論，後主深器之。

translations.literal: Jun Gong was broadly learned, talented in debate, and skilled at discussion; the Last Emperor valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Gong was learned, eloquent, and skilled in debate; the Last Emperor prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隋文帝以其叛己，命斬于建康。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui, because he had rebelled against Sui, ordered him beheaded at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui had him beheaded at Jiankang for rebelling against Sui.

sentences.zh: 後主貴妃張麗華

translations.literal: Last Emperor Noble Consort Zhang Lihua
translations.idiomatic: Last Emperor Noble Consort Zhang Lihua

sentences.zh: 魏徵補註

translations.literal: Wei Zheng's supplementary note
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng's supplementary note

sentences.zh: 史臣侍中鄭國公魏徵考覽記書，參詳故老，云後主初即位，以始興王叔陵之亂，被傷臥于承香閣下，時諸姬嵭不得進，唯張貴妃侍焉。

translations.literal: The historiographer, Palace Attendant and Duke of Zheng, Wei Zheng, examined records and consulted elders, saying: When the Last Emperor first took the throne, because of the disorder of Prince of Shixing Shuling, he was wounded and lay ill below the Hall of Accepting Fragrance; at that time none of the ladies could enter—only Noble Consort Zhang attended him.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer, palace attendant and Duke of Zheng, Wei Zheng, examined the records and consulted elders and wrote: When the Last Emperor first succeeded, he was wounded in the disorder of Prince of Shixing Shuling and lay ill below the Hall of Accepting Fragrance; none of the palace women could enter—only Noble Consort Zhang attended him.

sentences.zh: 而柳太后猶居柏梁殿，即皇后之正殿也。

translations.literal: Yet Empress Dowager Liu still dwelt in the Hall of Cypress Beam—that is, the empress's principal hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Empress Dowager Liu still lived in the Hall of Cypress Beam, the empress's proper hall.

sentences.zh: 後主沈皇后素無寵，不得侍疾，別居求賢殿。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor's Empress Shen had never been favored and could not attend his illness; she lived apart in the Hall of Seeking the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor's empress Shen had never been favored and could not nurse him; she lived apart in the Hall of Seeking the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，乃於光照殿前起臨春、結綺、望仙三閣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, before the Hall of Radiant Light he raised the three towers Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 (584) he raised the three towers Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian before the Hall of Radiant Light.

sentences.zh: [7]閣高數丈，嵭數十間，其窗牖、壁帶、懸楣、欄檻之類，嵭以沈檀香木為之，又飾以金玉，間以珠翠，外施珠簾，內有寶祷、寶帳，其服玩之屬，瑰奇珍麗，近古所未有。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 7. The towers were several zhang high, with dozens of bays; their windows, wall bands, hanging lintels, and balustrades were all made of agarwood, further adorned with gold and jade and set with pearls and kingfisher feathers; outside hung pearl curtains, within were jeweled canopies and jeweled curtains; their garments and ornaments were marvelous and rare, unmatched in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: [7] The towers stood several zhang high, with dozens of bays. Windows, wall bands, lintels, and balustrades were all of agarwood, adorned with gold, jade, pearls, and kingfisher feathers; pearl curtains hung without, jeweled canopies within; their dress and ornaments were wonders such as recent ages had never seen.

sentences.zh: 每微風暫至，香聞數里，朝日初照，光谟後庭。

translations.literal: Whenever a slight breeze passed, the fragrance was smelled for several li; when the morning sun first shone, light flooded the rear court.
translations.idiomatic: When a breeze stirred, the fragrance carried for miles; at first light the rear court blazed with radiance.

sentences.zh: 其下積石為山，引水為池，植以奇樹，雜以花藥。

translations.literal: Below they piled stone into mountains, led water into pools, planted strange trees, and mixed in flowers and herbs.
translations.idiomatic: Below they piled stone into hills, led water into pools, and planted rare trees and flowers.

sentences.zh: 後主自居臨春閣，張貴妃居結綺閣，龔、孔二貴嬪居望仙閣，嵭復道交相往來。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor himself dwelt in the Linchun Pavilion; Precious Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Pavilion; the two honored consorts Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Pavilion; elevated passageways linked them so they could come and go to one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor lived in the Linchun Pavilion, Precious Consort Zhang in the Jieqi Pavilion, and Honored Consorts Gong and Kong in the Wangxian Pavilion, with skyways connecting them for constant visits.

sentences.zh: 又有王、李二美人、張、薛二淑媛、袁昭儀、何婕妤、江脩容等七人，嵭有寵，遞代以遊其上。

translations.literal: There were also the two Beautiful Ladies Wang and Li, the two Fair Ladies Zhang and Xue, Lady Yuan the Zhaoyi, Lady He the Jieyu, Lady Jiang the Xiurong, and seven others in all—all favored, taking turns to feast and roam upon the pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Seven more held favor—the Beautiful Ladies Wang and Li, the Fair Ladies Zhang and Xue, Zhaoyi Yuan, Jieyu He, and Xiurong Jiang—who took turns feasting and strolling on the terraces.

sentences.zh: 以宮人有文學者袁大捨等為女學士。

translations.literal: Palace women of literary accomplishment, such as Yuan Dashe, were made female academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Learned palace women such as Yuan Dashe were appointed female academicians.

sentences.zh: 後主每引賓客對貴妃等遊宴，則使諸貴人及女學士與狎客共賦新詩，互相贈答，採其尤豔麗者以為曲詞，被以新聲，選宮女有容色者以千百數，令習而哥之，[8]分部迭進，持以相樂。

translations.literal: Whenever the Last Emperor led guests to feast with the Precious Consort and the others, he would have the various ladies and female academicians join intimates in composing new poems and exchanging verses; the most gorgeous were chosen for song lyrics, set to new tunes; palace women of pleasing looks were selected by the hundreds and thousands and made to study and sing them; [8] by sections they advanced in rotation, holding revel together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Last Emperor feasted with guests and the Precious Consort, he had the ladies and female academicians join familiar companions in new verse, trading lines; the finest were set as lyrics to new music, and hundreds or thousands of comely palace women were drilled to sing them—[8] sections took turns performing for the revel.

sentences.zh: 其曲有玉樹後庭花、臨春樂等，大指所歸，皆美張貴妃、孔貴嬪之容色也。

translations.literal: Among the tunes were "Jade Tree, Rear-Court Blossom" and "Linchun Joy"; their drift in general praised the looks of Precious Consort Zhang and Honored Consort Kong.
translations.idiomatic: Tunes such as "Jade Tree, Rear-Court Blossom" and "Linchun Joy" chiefly praised the beauty of Precious Consort Zhang and Honored Consort Kong.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「璧月夜夜滿，瓊樹朝朝新。

translations.literal: The gist runs: "The jade moon is full every night; the jeweled tree is fresh each dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The gist runs: "The jade moon is full every night; the jeweled tree is fresh each dawn.

sentences.zh: 」而張貴妃髮長七尺，鬒黑如漆，其光可鑒。

translations.literal: " Yet Precious Consort Zhang's hair was seven feet long, black as lacquer, its luster mirror-bright.
translations.idiomatic: " Precious Consort Zhang's hair was seven feet long, black as lacquer and bright enough to mirror one's face.

sentences.zh: 特聰惠，有神采，進止閑暇，容色端麗。

translations.literal: Exceptionally clever and spirited, dignified in bearing, her countenance proper and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: She was exceptionally clever and spirited, graceful in movement, with a proper and lovely face.

sentences.zh: 每瞻視盼睞，光采溢目，照谟左右。

translations.literal: Whenever she glanced or looked sidelong, brilliance overflowed her eyes and lit those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Each sidelong glance brimmed with light and lit the company around her.

sentences.zh: 常於閣上靚粧，臨于軒檻，宮中遙望，飄若神仙。

translations.literal: She often made up finely atop the pavilion and leaned from the balustrade; viewed from afar within the palace she seemed to drift like an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: She often dressed at the pavilion rail; seen from afar in the palace she seemed to float like an immortal.

sentences.zh: 才辯彊記，善候人主顏色。

translations.literal: Gifted in argument with a strong memory, skilled at reading the sovereign's mood.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and retentive, she was adept at reading the ruler's mood.

sentences.zh: 是時，後主怠於政事，百司啟奏，嵭因宦者蔡脫兒、李善度進請，[9]後主置張貴妃於膝上共決之。

translations.literal: At that time the Last Emperor neglected government; when the hundred offices submitted memorials they all reached him through the eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu; [9] he seated Precious Consort Zhang on his lap to decide them together.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor had grown slack in rule; memorials from every office came only through eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu—[9] and he set Precious Consort Zhang on his knee to decide them with him.

sentences.zh: 李、蔡所不能記者，貴妃嵭為條疏，無所遺脫。

translations.literal: What Li and Cai could not remember, the Precious Consort would set out in ordered lists, omitting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: What Li and Cai forgot, the Precious Consort would lay out in clear lists without omission.

sentences.zh: 由是益加寵異，冠絕後庭。

translations.literal: Hence favor grew still more extraordinary; she stood above all the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Favor grew still more singular, and she stood first in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 而後宮之家，不遵法度，有挂於理者，但求哀於貴妃，貴妃則令李、蔡先啟其事，而後從容為言之。

translations.literal: When households of the inner palace broke the law and were at fault in principle, they need only plead with the Precious Consort; she would have Li and Cai first report the matter, then calmly speak for them.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-palace families who broke the law would beg the Precious Consort's mercy; she had Li and Cai raise the case first, then spoke for them at leisure.

sentences.zh: 大臣有不從者，亦因而譖之，所言無不聽。

translations.literal: If ministers did not comply, she would slander them too; nothing she said went unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who resisted were slandered as well, and the ruler heard her every word.

sentences.zh: 於是張、孔之勢，薰灼四方，大臣執政，亦從風而靡。

translations.literal: Thus the power of Zhang and Kong scorched all directions; ministers in charge also bowed before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Kong's influence blazed everywhere, and ministers in power bent with the wind.

sentences.zh: 閹宦便佞之徒，內外交結，轉相引進，賄賂公行，賞罰無常，綱紀瞀亂矣。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and sycophants linked inside and outside, recommending one another in turn; bribes ran openly, rewards and punishments had no fixed rule, and order was utterly confused.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and flatterers joined court and harem, promoting one another; bribes were open, rewards and punishments erratic, and discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：詩表關雎之德，易箸乾坤之基，然夫婦之際，人道之大倫也。

translations.literal: The historian says: The Odes praise the virtue of the ospreys; the Book of Changes sets forth the foundation of Heaven and Earth—yet the relation of husband and wife is the great constant of human conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Odes honor the virtue of the ospreys and the Changes lay the base of Heaven and Earth, yet marriage is the chief bond of human life.

sentences.zh: 若夫作儷天則，燮贊王化，則宣太后有其懿焉。

translations.literal: As for matching Heaven's pattern and harmonizing royal transformation, Queen Dowager Xuan had such virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To pair with Heaven's norm and aid royal transformation—Queen Dowager Xuan had that excellence.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 昭容昭儀 北監本、汲本、殿本「昭儀」在「昭容」上。

translations.literal: Fair Lady Zhaorong / Lady Zhaoyi: in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions "Zhaoyi" stands above "Zhaorong."
translations.idiomatic: On "Zhaorong, Zhaoyi": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions place Zhaoyi above Zhaorong.

sentences.zh: 按《南史·后妃傳》序，梁武帝所制九嬪之序，「昭儀」在「昭容」上，陳制多襲梁，當以作「昭儀、昭容」為是。

translations.literal: Note: the preface to the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" in the History of the Southern Dynasties, on the nine consort ranks instituted by Emperor Wu of Liang, places "Zhaoyi" above "Zhaorong"; Chen institutions mostly followed Liang—the order Zhaoyi, Zhaorong is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Dynasties preface to the consorts' biographies lists Liang's nine ranks with Zhaoyi above Zhaorong; Chen largely followed Liang, so Zhaoyi, Zhaorong is correct.

translations.literal: (ling)
translations.idiomatic: (ling)

sentences.zh: [今]之所綴 據各本改。

translations.literal: [present] what is here compiled—changed according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[present] what is here compiled": emended per all editions.

sentences.zh: 封建

translations.literal: "establish-fief" (fengjian)
translations.idiomatic: On "fengjian (establish-fief)"

translations.literal: (cheng)
translations.idiomatic: (cheng)

sentences.zh: [城]縣侯 據《南史》改。

translations.literal: [cheng] county marquis—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[cheng] county marquis": emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按建城縣，漢侯邑。

translations.literal: Note: Jiancheng county was a Han marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng county was a Han enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 《太平寰宇記》引雷次宗《豫章記》云：「漢高帝置。

translations.literal: The Universal Gazetteer cites Lei Cizong's Record of Yuzhang: "Emperor Gaodi of Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: The Universal Gazetteer quotes Lei Cizong's Record of Yuzhang: "Emperor Gaodi of Han established it.

sentences.zh: 以其創建城邑，故曰建城。

translations.literal: Because he founded the city-settlement, it is called Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because he founded the settlement, it was called Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 」今漢志、表作「建成」，後漢志以下皆作「建城」。

translations.literal: " In the present Han Treatise and tables it reads Jiancheng (built-complete); from the Later Han Treatise onward all read Jiancheng (establish-city).
translations.idiomatic: " The Han Treatise and tables read Jiancheng (built-complete); from the Later Han Treatise on all read Jiancheng (establish-city).

sentences.zh: 後文后兄欽襲爵建城侯，亦作「建城」。

translations.literal: Later the younger brother of Empress Wen, Qin, inherited as Marquis of Jiancheng—there too it reads Jiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Wen's brother Qin inherited as Marquis of Jiancheng, likewise written Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 大業十一年薨於東都 按「十一年」南史作「十二年」。

translations.literal: "In the eleventh year of Daye died at the Eastern Capital"—note: the History of the Southern Dynasties reads twelfth year for eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: On "died at the Eastern Capital in Daye year eleven": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads year twelve.

sentences.zh: 猶是深被恩遇 「猶」各本作「由」。

translations.literal: "yet was deeply favored"—the character you in all editions reads you (by/from).
translations.idiomatic: On "yet was deeply favored": all editions read you (by) for you (still).

sentences.zh: 按由猶通。

translations.literal: Note: you and you are interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: You and you are used interchangeably here.

sentences.zh: 太建三年納為皇太子妃 按「太建三年」當依

translations.literal: "In the third year of Taijian taken in as crown prince's consort"—note: on "third year of Taijian" one should follow
translations.idiomatic: On "taken as crown prince's consort in Taijian year three": Taijian year three should follow

sentences.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉

translations.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

sentences.zh: 作「太建元年」。

translations.literal: which reads "first year of Taijian."
translations.idiomatic: which reads first year of Taijian.

sentences.zh: 〈沈君理傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Shen Junli〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Shen Junli〉

sentences.zh: 云太建二年高宗以君理女為皇太子妃，亦訛。

translations.literal: says that in Taijian year two the High Ancestor made Junli's daughter crown prince's consort—this too is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: says the High Ancestor made Junli's daughter crown prince's consort in Taijian year two—that too is wrong.

sentences.zh: 乃於光照殿前起臨春結綺望仙三閣 「光照殿」《南史·張貴妃傳》作「光昭殿」，《通鑑》同。

translations.literal: "Then before the Guangzhao Hall he raised the three pavilions Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian"—"Guangzhao Hall" in the Biography of Precious Consort Zhang in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Guangzhao Hall; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On "before Guangzhao Hall he raised Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian": the Southern Dynasties biography of Precious Consort Zhang and the Comprehensive Mirror read Guangzhao Hall.

sentences.zh: 令習而哥之「哥」殿本作「个」。

translations.literal: "ordered them to study and sing"—ge in the Palace edition reads ge (counter).
translations.idiomatic: On "ordered them to study and sing": the Palace edition reads ge (unit) for ge (sing).

sentences.zh: 按「哥」古「歌」字。

translations.literal: Note: ge is the ancient graph for song.
translations.idiomatic: Ge is the archaic form of the graph for song.

sentences.zh: 嵭因宦者蔡脫兒李善度進請 「蔡脫兒」《南史》作「蔡臨兒」。

translations.literal: "all through the eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu to present petitions"—"Cai Tuo'er" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Cai Lin'er.
translations.idiomatic: On "memorials came through eunuchs Cai Tuo'er and Li Shandu": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Cai Lin'er for Cai Tuo'er.
